exposure: Gestational age at induction (41+3 to 41+6 weeks compared to 42 weeks or more)
cohort: The study included 58,964 women in Sweden with one previous birth and uncomplicated singleton pregnancies delivered at or after 41 weeks + 3 days gestational age, between 1998 and 2014.
finding: Induction of labor in prolonged pregnancies was associated with an increased risk of emergency caesarean section and poor neonatal outcomes, including low Apgar score, neonatal death, and meconium aspiration.
mod_finding: The success rate of vaginal delivery after induction in the second labor was significantly influenced by the mode of delivery in the first labor, as well as diagnoses and conditions present at the first delivery.
